page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-2xCPU-4GB is a budget-oriented virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features two shared x86_64 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it does provide one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates that the shared CPU allocation limits overall performance. The server scored 783.18 in stress-ng single-core and 1545.08 in multi-core tests, placing both metrics in the bottom 10% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large-block read and write speeds of 12.62 GB/sec and 10.18 GB/sec respectively, which are categorized as poor. However, the server demonstrates average performance in specific tasks, such as Geekbench single-core operations (1862.0), text processing (2215.0), and bzip3 single-threaded decompression (8.99 GB/sec).

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers a low-cost entry point suitable for workloads that do not require continuous, high-performance compute resources. The primary tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation, which leads to weaker multi-core scaling and lower database performance, as seen in the Passmark database score of 1356.4 and Redis SET operations at 2.65 million operations per second.

This server is best suited for lightweight, non-critical workloads. Appropriate use cases include basic web serving, small-scale text processing, software development testing, and running lightweight background utilities that can tolerate shared CPU resource contention.
